rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for multimodal performance. This tests combining RNA (PCA) and image (ResNet50) data with simple concatenation fusion, isolating the impact of multimodal integration. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines, addressing a key design choice with minimal complexity.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieves 0.526 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It is the best next step because it directly compares a key design choice (fusion type) in the same model setting and encoder configuration, providing efficient insight into whether weighted fusion could yield better results than concatenation.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~52.6% accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile (a key design choice) with avgpool aggregation, isolating its impact while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method consistent. It directly addresses whether multiprofile settings improve performance, which is critical for understanding the value of profile aggregation in this task.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, and avgpool aggregation achieve high accuracy (0.6186). This experiment tests the effect of fusion method (weighted vs concat) on the same base configuration, isolating the impact of fusion to determine if it improves performance. This is the best use of the next experiment as it directly addresses a key design choice (fusion) with minimal changes, leveraging the strong baseline from config_018.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve high performance. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l in the same setup, isolating the impact of the image encoder's complexity. It balances exploitation of the promising multiprofile direction with exploration of a more advanced image encoder, which may reveal if increased model capacity improves performance without altering other critical design choices.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve high performance. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (while keeping RNA encoder, image encoder, profile setting, and fusion method constant) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation. This is critical for determining if more complex aggregation methods yield gains, balancing exploration of key design choices with exploitation of current promising directions.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (as in config_019) yield the highest validation accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated representation) improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. It directly extends the most promising configuration while minimizing changes, efficiently reducing uncertainty about a key design decision.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_031) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing ResNet50 with imagenet_vit_l image encoder (a stronger encoder) further improves performance, isolating the effect of the image encoder while keeping other components consistent. This addresses uncertainty about the relative impact of image encoders on multimodal performance.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_037) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt (a more complex RNA encoder) while keeping other components fixed, isolating the impact of the RNA representation. It balances exploitation (building on a strong baseline) and exploration (testing a novel encoder), and avoids changing multiple variables simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l achieve high accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests whether RNA-only models with scvi_n200 (a high-performing encoder in multimodal setups) and multiprofile settings can match this performance, isolating the impact of modality choice. It addresses uncertainty about RNA-only viability while leveraging a proven encoder, balancing exploration and exploitation.
